answer.text:
On startup Paws does not blanket-restart in-flight items. `startPaws` calls `recoverOnStartup(db)` early in its startup sequence (`src/index.ts:376`), before the orchestration wiring that follows it (`src/index.ts:377-379`), and that function makes a per-item decision inside one `immediate` transaction so the state change and the follow-up jobs commit together (`src/db/recovery.ts:51`)(`src/db/decisions.ts:17-20`). The docs describe the same intent: a restart is safe while work is running, runners keep working while Paws is down and retain their results, and Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks (`README.md:54`).

The sweep first shifts runner leases so Paws downtime (up to an `offlineBudgetMs` budget) is not charged against an open runner lease (`src/db/recovery.ts:44`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:52`), then loads every item in `awaiting_input`, `running`, `verifying`, `recovering` or `merge_queue` (`src/db/recovery.ts:53`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:31-37`). For each item it skips the ones already accounted for: an item with a standing restart question gets `ask_restart` immediately and the loop continues (`src/db/recovery.ts:58-61`); an item with a parked runner-capacity wait is left alone, because the code's comment says it already has its next attempt and restarting would neither spend a recovery attempt nor add a job (`src/db/recovery.ts:62`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:103-114`); and items with a pending answer-resume or pending transient retry are skipped too (`src/db/recovery.ts:63-64`). Only then does it gather evidence for the decision: whether the runner still holds the work, whether a row still exists in `merge_call` (meaning a merge call may have been in flight) (`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80`), whether a run is still active, and how long ago the item was last resumed (`src/db/recovery.ts:65-74`)(`src/db/items.ts:57-59`).

`decideStartup` then applies the rules in order (`src/core/recovery.ts:84-106`). States outside the resumable set get `none` (`src/core/recovery.ts:93`). An item in `merge_queue` whose run is not still active keeps its place in the queue, with a flag recording whether a merge call may have been in flight so the merge job first asks GitHub whether it actually went through; a merge-queue item whose run was still active instead re-verifies (`src/core/recovery.ts:94-96`). A checkpoint showing a merge was in progress, or a verifying item whose runner still holds its Closeout review or check run, re-verifies (`src/core/recovery.ts:97-98`). An item whose runner holds work is resumed in a fresh session from its checkpoint and flagged to reattach to the existing runner work (`src/core/recovery.ts:99-100`). Otherwise, an item already resumed once and resumed less than `RESUME_AGAIN_AFTER_MS` ago gets `ask_restart`, which the recovery test describes as ruling out a crash loop; a verifying item with a verification candidate re-verifies; everything else resumes in a fresh session from its checkpoint or, without one, from its branch (`src/core/recovery.ts:101-105`)(`src/core/recovery.test.ts:92-109`). The other tests pin the merge-queue cases (keep place with and without `mergeCallInFlight`, re-verify when `runActive`) and the re-verify of a queued item cut short (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:122-152`), and show a verifying item whose runner lease ran past its grace re-verifying once (enqueuing a `run.reverify` job with `recheckHead`) and then getting `ask_restart` with no `run.resume` on the next start (`test/runner-closeout-restart.test.ts:457-477`).

`applyDecision` turns each decision into durable effects: `resume` calls `applyResume` with the checkpoint and reattach flag, `reverify` calls `applyReverify` (passing whether it was resumed), `keep_place` calls `applyKeepPlace` with the merge-call flag, and `ask_restart` calls `applyAskRestart`, with an exhaustive default that throws on an unknown decision (`src/db/decisions.ts:28-47`). Two decisions are deliberately not applied: if a resume would reattach and a `process_restart` resume is already pending, or if a re-verify would attach to a runner's still-open Closeout work (holds, state `verifying`, an open re-verify), Paws lets the existing job do the work instead of enqueueing a duplicate (`src/db/recovery.ts:75-86`). Resume run-at times are spaced 5 seconds apart via `STARTUP_RESUME_SPACING_MS` and passed as `runAt` so a pile of recovered items does not all start at once (`src/db/recovery.ts:56`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:84-85`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:39`); the stagger test aborts the first loop, calls `prepareShutdown` (leaving every item in `recovering`), then calls `recoverOnStartup` and runs the loops until all four implementations have started, advancing a fake clock when nothing is in flight (`test/startup-resume-stagger.test.ts:147-184`).

`awaiting_input` items are part of the startup state list and go through the same decision loop, then are handled again afterwards: any run capacity held by their `currentRunId` is released, and if there was at least one such item a `catchup` job with reason `open_questions` is enqueued once per startup timestamp (`src/db/recovery.ts:53`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:89-98`). A unit test is named for leaving a parked question where it is (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:154-156`). One adjacent mechanism worth knowing: once an item is running, `restart()` is fenced by a durable merge marker and returns null while a merge call is unsettled, so an in-flight merge is never torn down by a restart (`test/restart-ask.test.ts:49-67`).
caveats: The research note says inspection stopped at the deep-pass limit; the bodies of applyResume/applyReverify/applyKeepPlace/applyAskRestart, the RESUMABLE set and the value of RESUME_AGAIN_AFTER_MS are not in the evidence.

Whether recoverOnStartup runs strictly before startLoops/startHost is not directly shown: the evidence shows the call inside startPaws and the definitions of the loops, not the loop start-up lines in the same function.

The docs' claim about reattaching to in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks [E3:54] is only partly corroborated by code here: the reattach and attached-job logic plus the runner-held re-verify rule are visible, but not the full answer-task path.
For E17:154-156 only the test name and the start of the decideStartup call are visible, not its expected decision.
No evidence shows startup behavior for states outside STARTUP_STATES (for example queued or failed items).
